chapter: Rhythm Club memories and playing technique
title: Harlem stride pianists and after-hours jam spots

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Wish I could dig that up.
Cliff Jackson was another name that...
Oh yeah, Cliff Jackson, Don Frye, they were-- Willie Gant. Corky Williams, have you ever heard of him?
Yeah, Corky Williams was another great pianist. Stride piano. He was there with Willie the Lion and Willie Gant, Corky Williams. Another one name of Price Jones. Dick Edwards.
I forgot to ask you yesterday when you were doing those rent parties, you were very young, did you run into Fats Waller and James P. Johnson at those?

Oh yeah, oh yeah. James P. Of course as you see I've made records with James P. I never made any, didn't make any records with Fats. But oh yeah, Fats Waller, they used to have those sessions, they used to be an after hour place there on 132nd Street and everybody used to go there and have those piano jam sessions and Willie the Lion Smith used to come in smoking his cigar, he was very braggadocious like, he'd just walk in you know and somebody's sit down there at the piano and he would walk in and everybody would say uh uh, there's Willie the Lion, and he would scare just a beginning piano player out of the chair. Holler at him, 'Get up off that piano, boy, you don't know what you're doing. Listen to this. Get up there, boy,' he'd jump up and Willie the Lion Smith would sit down there and start striding. Another good pianist was a pianist that was with Chick Webb, Kirk Patrick and Joe Steele. Joe Steele had an arrangement on 'Coalyard Shuffle' was the darnedest thing you ever heard. They were all good piano players.
And they would all make those sessions.

Oh yeah, sit around there, Fats Waller, Corky Williams, Willie Gant, Dick Edwards, Price Jones, all of them would be there. Not only piano players, there would be other musicians, drummers, saxophones, trombones
That was at the Band Box. Oh, this club where they used to jam?
